title: Heroic Teacher and Armed Father Confront Gunman to Stop Oregon School Shooting
snippet: Quick intervention by a courageous teacher and an armed parent halted a deadly shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, preventing further loss of life.
content:
BEND, Ore. — A deadly assault at an Oregon elementary school was prevented from turning into an even greater catastrophe thanks to the swift, selfless actions of an educator and an armed parent, local authorities announced Friday.

The suspect, identified by police as 16-year-old Griffin J. John II, launched an attack on a special-needs classroom at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend. Armed with a 12-gauge shotgun, the teenager killed 25-year-old teacher Meghan Lambert and three young children, ages 5, 8, and 11. Another 7-year-old child and a second teacher suffered severe injuries during the violence.

Selfless Bravery in the Classroom

As the gunman opened fire inside the classroom, an unidentified female teacher took immediate action to protect her students. She hurled her phone at the shooter before tackling him to the floor and physically engaging him. Moments later, 36-year-old Kaylub Giamanco, a parent of two students attending the school, rushed into the room armed with a legally owned handgun and fatally shot the assailant.

"The teacher who was willing to stand and fight for her children, that's true heroism," Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said through visible emotion during a press briefing. Krantz credited both individuals with saving numerous lives, noting that the gunman still had dozens of unspent rounds on him when he was stopped.

A Community Seeking Answers

Investigators revealed that the suspect threw his weapon over a perimeter fence before breaching locked glass doors to enter the building. While police arrived on the scene within three minutes of the initial distress call, the threat had already been neutralized by Giamanco.

As the Bend community mourns the heartbreak at Silver Rail Elementary, memorials of flowers and candles have poured in near the school grounds. Lambert's family released a statement honoring her lifelong dream of teaching special-needs children and praised the heroism of those who risked their lives to protect others.
